why: Drawing 3600 marks a plain turn-up-free hem line above a clean bottom edge; the photo shows a single-fold plain hem with no cuff band, no topstitching, sharp front crease running to the raw edge — construction class matches exactly.

Blueprint 3604 places the hem marker high enough for a turn-up and the photo shows a genuine single external cuff with a distinct folded lip and shadow line at its top edge; cuff depth reads slightly deeper than 4.4 cm relative to leg opening, but the construction (single turn-up cuff) is correct.

The shipped photo RENDERS an explicit dimension callout reading 7cm above the hem edge — annotation text traced from the drawing into the photograph. Annotations are manufacturing documentation and must never render in a customer-facing photo (standing rule). Construction (plain uncuffed hem) otherwise matches drawing 3608, so the regeneration is an annotation fix, not a geometry fix.

Blueprint 3609 marks a plain hem allowance with no turn-up; the navy photo shows a clean plain hem, no cuff fold, no topstitch, correct single front crease. Exact 7.6 cm allowance depth is internal and not measurable in the photo.

Drawing 360H shows the deepest plain-hem marker with no cuff geometry; the charcoal photo is likewise a plain uncuffed hem with unbroken fabric to the edge. Construction agrees; the 9.0 cm allowance is an interior dimension not verifiable externally.

Blueprint 3602 sets the turn-up marker very close to the hem edge for a shallow cuff; the photo shows a real external turn-up with the folded lip and a horizontal seam line at the cuff top. Cuff present and shallow, though 3.2 vs 3.8 cm is not separable by eye.

Drawing 3603 marks a turn-up hem; the photo shows a single external cuff of roughly 3.8 cm against the leg opening, fold edge and cuff-top crease clearly visible. Correct single turn-up, no double fold.

Drawing 360K is the only one in the batch with a slanted hem marker; the photo shows no external cuff and an interior fold crease about 4 cm up whose slope (~9°) is steeper than perspective slant in sibling photos, indicating an angled fold. Slant direction vs the shoe toe is ambiguous, so the angle orientation is unconfirmed.

The 1661418 blueprint shows a fixed plain bottom with a stitch line just above the edge; the photo is the only one in the batch with a visible parallel topstitch band ~2.5 cm above the hem edge and no turn-up, matching the fixed-bottom topstitched construction.
